plate_comment: Calculates the rail pressure setpoint fuel_pressure_setpoint (0.0488 MPa per count; this is its only writer) in the auxiliary-control task: the lower of the blended rpm x fuel quantity map (fuel_pressure_setpoint_base_map / _map_1 to _map_4), the coolant limit and the ambient limit (their sum when the byte at 0x409a71 is 0; it is 1 here) plus a slewed offset table, held in a dead band at low speed and load. While cranking it uses the cold-start table and then ramps out of it, and the result is clamped to the calibration minimum and maximum (3279 counts = 160 MPa here); a forced or additive override, 0 while engine_starting, a fixed value in governor_speed_limit_mode 1 and the fault-reaction cap (fault_reaction_request_bits bit 2) also act on it. The winning term goes to fuel_pressure_setpoint_winning_term_code (was cm848_sensor_channel_state_load).
evidence: xref of 0x40b8b6: all 10 stores are in this function; its tables are the fuel_pressure_setpoint_* family (map values 717-3279 counts = 35-160 MPa over rpm x fuel quantity). Called from cm848_periodicTaskSet_auxiliaryControl; the RAM dump reproduces it: setpoint 1000 = the cold-start table at 32 F and 0 rpm (819 at 0 F, 1045 at 40 F), winning term 6, DAT_0040b8be 717 = the map at its axis minimum.

plate_comment: Monitors the fuel metering output feedback against the governor demand: while the rail pressure is within 61 counts of fuel_pressure_setpoint at the governor setpoint, between fuel_pressure_feedback_minimum and _maximum, with the coolant at 180-205 F and no related fault, it adds the pressure gain table, the coolant table and the rpm table into a governor demand threshold, looks up the minimum fuel_metering_feedback_input expected at that threshold, and sets fault 60 (P1223) when the feedback has been below it for 150 net passes. The live-demand residual only replaces the constant 41 when the byte at 0x409aba is 0; it is 41 in this calibration, so that branch is not active. (was engine_camTiming_positionCorrection_calc, not cam timing)
evidence: Compares fuel_metering_feedback_input with fuel_metering_feedback_min_by_demand_threshold(DAT_0040b8ea) and sets fault_detected_bits_48_to_63 0x1000 = fault 60 = slot 164 = P1223 (ROM 0x5985a decode); nothing here is cam timing. The meaning of P1223 itself is not established. Medium-high: the fault condition and tables are clear, the physical feedback signal (QADC slot 63) is still unidentified.

plate_comment: Rail pressure diagnostics, run in cm848_phase_group_b_processing right after cm848_calculateFuelMeteringCommand while cold_start_phase is at the governor setpoint and the pressure sensor has no confirmed fault: it sets up to seven bits of fuel_pressure_diagnostic_flags (pressure above the too-high threshold for 150 passes, above a second range limit, below the rpm table minimum, above or below the setpoint while the governor demand is low or high, below the leak-down model or demand above its limit with no fuel, demand above 283 with governor mode 11 at its target speed), debounces them into fuel_pressure_diagnostic_snapshot (150 passes) and sets the fault bits. Only the too-high bit (fault 303, P0088) has an OBD code; the other six go to fault bits 315, 323, 316, 317, 290 and 324, which have no OBD slot. (was cm848_processEnginePositionDiagnostics)
evidence: Fault 303 (fault_detected_bits_288_to_303 0x8000) = slot 90 = P0088 comes only from the too-high bit; the others are slot 170 (no OBD code) and 317 / 290 / 324 feed fault_reaction_request_bits in cm848_protectionInputValidator. Every table it reads is a fuel_pressure_* table and it runs between the metering command and the PWM output; this function does not set the P1222 / P1223 faults (those are the other two monitors).

plate_comment: Rail pressure checks that run only while the injection quantity engine_timing_reference is not above the limit at 0x409ac0 (0, so no fuel is injected), above 800 rpm, with fuel_pressure_feedback_filtered between its minimum and maximum, the coolant at 180-205 F and no related fault. Check A (enabled here) compares fuel_pressure_governor_demand with a limit looked up from the pressure (fuel_pressure_governor_demand_plausibility_limit_*, 255-434) and sets fault 58 (P1222) after 80 net passes above it; check B (switched off here by the byte at 0x409aa2) compares the pressure with a decaying model and sets fault 59 (slot 158, code 0000). (was engine_camSync_referenceCheck_update)
evidence: cam_sync_refA_required_count is the demand limit looked up from fuel_pressure_feedback_filtered (axis 1025-2869 counts, values 255-434) and compared with fuel_pressure_governor_demand; fault bits 58 / 59 = slots 163 / 158 (P1222 / code 0000). The lead pairing it with P0088 is wrong: P0088 is set only by cm848_processEnginePositionDiagnostics. engine_timing_reference is the per-injection fuel quantity (written by engine_injectionAngle_updateCutoutAndTimingDemand from fuel demand x timing fraction). Check B is off (0x409aa2 = 0) and its decay step table 0x409b16 is all zero, so its names rest on code only.

plate_comment: Limits the fuel quantity when the rail pressure cannot follow its setpoint (enabled by bit 1 of protection_config_flags_b): once fuel_demand_computed is above the rpm table limit (fuel_quantity_limit_rail_pressure_shortfall_values) while fuel_pressure_setpoint minus fuel_pressure_sensor is at least 512 counts (25 MPa) for 2500 consecutive passes, it arms a ramp that falls 1 count per pass from fuel_demand_load_axis to the table value and holds there, and lowers protection_fuel_limit_active to the ramp with governor_fuel_mode_command 61. Only the feature-disabled branch writes the armed flag back to 0. (was protection_fuel_demand_limiting)
evidence: Table input is current_rpm (14400-28000 counts = 1800-3500 rpm) and its output 1855 down to 1119 (126 to 76 mm3 per stroke) is compared with fuel_demand_computed; arming test, debounce 2500, ramp step 1 and threshold 512 are the RAM-dump constants at 0x408984 / 0x408980 / 0x408982. Called from cm848_processProtectionLimits; the four state words are used only here and in protection_speed_limit_initialize (resets the ramp to 0x1700).

Written only by the setpoint calculator (10 stores) and its init (1 store): 1 engine starting (setpoint 0), 2 map, 3 coolant limit, 4 ambient limit, 5 forced override, 6 cold-start table, 7 sum mode, 8-11 = 2 / 3 / 4 / 7 with the offset active, 12 / 13 = ramp up / down out of the cold-start value, 14 maximum clamp, 15 fault-reaction cap, 16 / 17 minimum clamp (cranking / running); 6 in the RAM dump. cm848_updateEngineStatusFlags packs it as byte 1 of engine_timing_arb_status_packed.

Dword store, only here: fuel_pressure_setpoint_offset_grid(engine_rpm_measured, fuel_demand_computed) x 100 (grid values 0 / 102 / 205 counts = 0 / 5 / 10 MPa). It is slewed into 0x3fd0c6 and the setpoint adds slewed / 100, only in governor modes 0x10 / 0x32 / 0x3a with coolant above 180 F and intake manifold temperature above 70 F. The x 100 should go in the CSV comment.

disasm_func: 8 accesses, all lwz / stw, so a dword (x 100) although typed word (the .cpp renders _cam_timing_advance_slew_working, which is why xref_addr finds no function); only the setpoint calculator uses it: it steps toward fuel_pressure_setpoint_offset_target by the slew step each pass and back to 0 when the offset conditions end.
RAM copy of a ROM constant (4098 in the dump = 40.98 counts per pass in the x 100 unit of the offset); only the setpoint calculator reads it.

Cold-start hand-over state of the setpoint (only the calculator and its init hpcr_register_state_save use it): 1 = cranking phases / waiting, 2 = follow the running value, 4 = ramping up by the step, 8 = ramping down; needs protection_feature_flags bit 4; 1 in the dump.
RAM copy of a ROM constant (1 count per pass in the dump); added to or subtracted from fuel_pressure_setpoint in transition states 4 / 8; read only by the setpoint calculator.

Not a rate limiter: when the candidate is more than the band above the stored value it becomes candidate - band, when more than the band below it becomes candidate + band, otherwise it holds - a dead-band follower. It is used (and DAT_0040b8c4 = 1) only below 1500 rpm and 50 mm3 per stroke; the dump is consistent with it: running value 677 = 717 - 40 (717 is the map value; I did not print the coolant / ambient limit terms or this word).
RAM copy of a ROM constant (40 counts = 1.95 MPa) used as the +/- band of the dead-band follower above (not a per-pass rate); read only by the setpoint calculator.

The candidate after the low-speed dead band and the rise limit (rise limit = previous setpoint + 0x409a78), before the cold-start table / transition and the final clamp; the old comment 'rate-limited' is wrong. Used only by the setpoint calculator; 677 in the dump.

Byte, 0 in the dump: 1 returns at once with fuel_pressure_setpoint = the override value (winning term 5), 2 adds the value to the final setpoint (flag DAT_0040b8c8). Only the setpoint calculator reads it; a RAM copy of ROM, so no _cal.
Word at an odd address (0 in the dump), the value forced or added by fuel_pressure_setpoint_override_mode; only the setpoint calculator reads it.

Output of the fuel_metering_feedback_min_by_demand_threshold lookup at the demand threshold (1391 at 0 falling to 0 at 2869); the monitor counts passes with fuel_metering_feedback_input below it. Used only by the monitor.
Up / down counter (+1 while the feedback is below the minimum, -1 otherwise, capped at the limit); fault 60 is set when it reaches the limit and cleared at 0. Used only by the monitor.
RAM copy of a ROM constant, 150 in the dump; the cap and trip value of the counter above.

(governor demand - coolant offset - rpm offset) x 41 / divisor, clamped to +/-32767 and held between updates (updated only while at the governed speed with the vehicle stopped); that branch is not active in this calibration (0x409aba nonzero). It is an instantaneous scaled residual, not a P controller and not a cam timing correction; 0 in the dump.
Lookup of fuel_pressure_governor_demand_threshold_gain_* at fuel_pressure_feedback_filtered (316-516 over 1025-2869 counts); with the residual fixed at 41 the scaled term equals this gain.
Lookup of fuel_pressure_governor_demand_residual_divisor_* at the filtered pressure (all zero here), x 100 and at least 1, used as the divisor of the residual; it is a divisor, not a time constant.
2-D lookup (coolant temperature x filtered rail pressure) in fuel_pressure_governor_demand_offset_coolant_*; subtracted from the demand in the residual. Used only by the monitor.
2-D lookup (coolant x filtered rail pressure) in fuel_pressure_governor_demand_threshold_coolant_*; added into the demand threshold. Used only by the monitor.
2-D lookup (rpm x engine_timing_reference, the injection quantity) in fuel_pressure_governor_demand_offset_rpm_*; subtracted from the demand in the residual. Used only by the monitor.
2-D lookup (rpm x injection quantity) in fuel_pressure_governor_demand_threshold_rpm_*; added into the demand threshold. Used only by the monitor.

Recomputed every pass: pressure within +/-61 counts of the setpoint (0x409ab6 / 0x409ab8) at the governor setpoint, pressure and coolant in range, no related faults; the monitor returns when it is 0. Used only by the monitor.

Engine speed within governor_speed_limit_output +/- 160 counts (20 rpm), vehicle_speed_copy 0 and the vehicle speed sensor ok; it only gates the residual update, which is not active in this calibration.

Output of the fuel_pressure_governor_demand_plausibility_limit_* lookup at fuel_pressure_feedback_filtered (255 at 1025 counts to 434 at 2869), compared with fuel_pressure_governor_demand; it is a limit, not a count. Used only by check A.
Set when fuel_pressure_governor_demand is above the plausibility limit (check A); used only there.
Up / down counter (+1 above the limit, -1 otherwise, cap = limit); fault 58 is set at the cap and cleared at 0.
RAM copy of a ROM constant, 80 in the dump; used only by check A.
Calibration byte, 1 in the dump: check A (demand against the plausibility limit) is enabled; the function returns at once when both check enable bytes are 0.
Calibration byte, 0 in the dump: check B (pressure against a decaying model) is switched off in this calibration; its names rest on code only.

Both checks are disabled when engine_timing_reference (the per-injection fuel quantity, not a timing) is above this value; 0 in the dump, so they run only with no fuel injected. The old name said timing and minimum.

Check B only (not the feedback monitor): base (the latched pressure, then the previous model) minus the allowed decay step; fault 59 counts passes with fuel_pressure_feedback_filtered below it; DAT_0040b8dc is a copy of it. Check B is off here and the step table is all zero, so confirmed from code only.
Check B only: fuel_pressure_feedback_filtered latched every pass until the check conditions have held for the debounce, then seeds the model (cam_timing_correction_base).
Check B only: lookup of fuel_pressure_allowed_decay_step_* at the model base (all zero here), subtracted from the base each pass.

Only user is the rail pressure diagnostics: copies fuel_pressure_sensor while the governor demand or the fuel demand is nonzero, otherwise falls each pass by the fuel_pressure_expected_decay_by_pressure_* lookup; flag 0x20 when the sensor is below it. A modelled rail pressure, not a cam sync reference.
Last pass's value of the model; the input of the decay lookup. Only user is the rail pressure diagnostics.

Bits: 1 too high (via the pending flag), 2 above the second range limit, 4 below the rpm minimum, 8 above setpoint with low demand, 0x10 below setpoint with high demand, 0x20 below the leak-down model or demand above its limit with no fuel, 0x40 demand above the idle limit. Users: the diagnostics, cm848_updateEngineDiagnosticCounters, cm848_initEngineDiagnosticData. Not the same variable as 0x40b8cc engine_position_diag_flags.

Debounced copy of the flags OR-ed with the pending flag; read by the three monitors as 'no rail pressure diagnostic active', by cm848_protectionSensorFaultHandler (bits 1 / 2 request logical output 54 when engine_position_fault_enable_cal is set) and stored in the fault freeze frame (fault_entry_t.diagnostic_byte_4 and DAT_003fe81b).

Bit 0 only: set after the pressure was above the too-high threshold for the limit count; cleared when the engine stops, feature bit 0x2000 is off, or after the recovery count; OR-ed into the snapshot without the debounce. Users: the diagnostics and the init function.
3688 counts (180 MPa; the sensor full scale is 3689). RAM copy of ROM at 0x4095xx, outside the EEPROM mirror 0x3fd482-0x3feec1, so no _cal. Only the diagnostics read it.
Counts passes with fuel_pressure_sensor above the too-high threshold up to the limit byte (150), then sets the pending flag; reset with the pending flag. Users: the diagnostics and the init function.
Counts passes with the pressure back below the threshold; at the recovery limit (500) the pending flag and the too-high count reset. Users: the diagnostics and the init function.
Counted in cm848_updateEngineDiagnosticCounters on passes where the flags are 0 but the snapshot is not; above 150 (0x40951c) the snapshot takes the flags. Not an engine sync counter.
Counted on passes where the flags are nonzero and differ from the snapshot; above 150 (0x40951a) the snapshot takes the flags.

30738 in the dump; flag 2 (fault 315, no OBD slot) is set when fuel_pressure_sensor is above it, so it is a second, higher limit (the old 'lower' is wrong) that cannot trip within the sensor's 3689-count range; its purpose is not clear. RAM copy of ROM: no _cal. No name proposed.
204 counts (10 MPa): the below-minimum-for-rpm test (flag 4) only applies above it. RAM copy of ROM: no _cal.

283 (6.9 % of 4095): flag 0x40 needs fuel_pressure_governor_demand above it with governor mode 11 near its target speed, the vehicle stopped and the coolant above 0x409526 (the 'idle' in the name assumes governor mode 11 is idle, which the repo only calls probable). Same value as cam_timing_speed_window_reference_count_threshold (0x409ad0). RAM copy of ROM: no _cal.

11200 = 175 F (1/64 F per count): the governor mode 11 demand test (flag 0x40) needs the coolant above it ('idle' in the name assumes mode 11 is idle, which the repo only calls probable). RAM copy of ROM: no _cal.
500 passes below the threshold reset the pending flag. RAM copy of ROM: no _cal.
150 in the dump; trip value of the set debounce count. RAM copy of ROM: no _cal.
150 in the dump; trip value of the clear debounce count. RAM copy of ROM: no _cal.
Read as a byte in the diagnostics (._0_1_): the value is 150 (the word 0x9600 includes the next byte); typed word, see the type note. RAM copy of ROM: no _cal.
The limiter's falling quantity ramp (starts at fuel_demand_load_axis, holds at the table value); 0x1700 = 5888 when not armed. Users: only the limiter and protection_speed_limit_initialize.
Set when the shortfall debounce completes; the only write that clears it (no clearing write found otherwise) is the feature-disabled branch. All 4 accesses are in the limiter.
Consecutive passes with fuel_demand_computed above the table limit and a pressure shortfall of at least 512 counts; reset on any failing pass; arms at 2500. Used only by the limiter.
Set when the ramp reaches the table value, after which the ramp is held at the table value. Used only by the limiter.

Not the rail pressure flags (those are 0x3fb6e0): written by cm848_updateProtectionBitFlags, which I did not read, and read by the injection-angle cylinder selection / cut-out code, mpc555_evaluateProtectionSyncFaults and the three monitors as a 'no fault' gate. The same holds for protection_fault_status_a / b / c (0x40b8cd-0x40b8cf). No name proposed.

text: Fault decode (ROM 0x5985a slot table, then obd_dtc_code_table; fault n = word n / 16 bit n % 16): bit 57 (word 3 mask 0x200) = slot 162 = P1221, 58 (0x400) = slot 163 = P1222, 59 (0x800) = slot 158 (code 0000), 60 (0x1000) = slot 164 = P1223, 303 = slot 90 = P0088. The meanings of P1221-P1223 are not established. The other bits set by 0x49264 (290, 315, 316, 317, 323, 324) are slot 170: no OBD slot. 317 / 290 / 324 (and 408 from hpcr_camTimingMonitor) feed fault_reaction_request_bits through cm848_protectionInputValidator (0x49df0, its cold_start_*_mask_cal words are misnamed). The comment of fault_reaction_request_bits (0x40b8a0) still says bit 2 caps cam_timing_measured: that is now fuel_pressure_setpoint, capped at DAT_0040953e (4095 here, so no cap).

Sibling function, not in my lead list: engine_camTiming_speedWindow_update (0x52a9ac) is the third monitor of this group (fault 57 = P1221). It is switched off in this calibration (byte 0x409aa0 = 0); when enabled, with engine speed within governor_speed_limit_output +/- 160 counts, vehicle_speed_copy 0, cold_start_phase at the governor setpoint, coolant 180-205 F and no related faults, it debounces (80 net passes) fuel_pressure_governor_demand above cam_timing_speed_window_reference_count_threshold (283). Suggested name cm848_checkFuelPressureGovernorDemandAtGovernedSpeed; its variables cam_timing_speed_window_* (0x40b8d4 debounce count, 0x40b906 / 0x40b907 flags, 0x409aac / 0x409ad0 / 0x409ad2 constants, DAT_0040b908) are fuel pressure names too, and 0x409aaa is a ROM constant compared with engine_timing_reference.

Sibling functions: hpcr_register_state_save (0x52a910) is the init of the setpoint calculator (cam_timing_transition_state = 1, winning term code = 1, the 2-D lookup cache words 0x3fd0ca-0x3fd0e8 = 2): suggested cm848_initFuelPressureSetpointState (cam_timing_advance_table_interp_states 0x3fd0ca is the first of those cache words). cm848_calibration_group28_load (0x52b998) only calls the three monitors (suggested cm848_runFuelPressureGovernorMonitors) and cm848_initialization_group28_state (0x52b9c0) sets their 13 cache words 0x3fd0ea-0x3fd102 to 2 (suggested cm848_initFuelPressureGovernorMonitorState).

hpcr_camTimingMonitor (0x531d34, its reset hpcr_camTimingReset 0x532208) is a rail pressure tracking monitor, not cam timing: each cycle it integrates (fuel_pressure_setpoint - fuel_pressure_feedback_previous) / the ROM divisor at 0x64420 into cam_timing_advance_accumulator (0x40b9d8) and, negated, cam_timing_retard_accumulator (0x40b9dc) via cam_timing_delta_per_cycle (0x40b9e0); above the ROM limits 0x6440e / 0x64412 it sets fault bits 408 / 409 (fault_detected_bits_400_to_415 0x100 / 0x200; ROM 0x5985a decode: both are slot 91 = P0148) and cam_timing_monitor_state (0x40b9e2) 3. Its cam_timing_monitor_* names and these accumulators should be re-domained with the rest. Not read in full.

Support code around cm848_processEnginePositionDiagnostics, names suspect: cm848_updateEngineDiagnosticCounters (0x49a54) holds the two debounce counters of the diagnostics and also the fuel metering feedback circuit check (faults 264 / 265, fuel_metering_feedback_fault_code); cm848_initEngineDiagnosticData (0x4a258) initialises these variables and the seven lookup cache words cam_sync_filter_init_state_0-6 (0x3fb6ce-0x3fb6da; DAT_003fb6cc is the eighth, used by the feedback input lookup) - suggested fuel_pressure_diagnostic_interpolation_state_0-6; cm848_protectionSensorFaultHandler (0x49edc) picks fuel limits for P0192 / P0193 / fault 264 / P0251 / P0088 and requests logical output 54 on the too-high bits; cm848_checkProtectionFaultConditions (0x4a114) builds engine_sync_fault_active_flag (0x40b8a8) from faults 264 / 265 / 333 / 304 / 305 / 303 and reaction bits 1 / 2 masked by engine_sync_enable_mask.

Setpoint calculator constants and flags without CSV rows (or with DAT_ names), suggested names: DAT_0040b8c4 fuel_pressure_setpoint_deadband_active_flag (1 below DAT_00409a82 = 12000 = 1500 rpm and DAT_00409a80 = 736 = 50 mm3 per stroke; write-only), DAT_0040b8c6 fuel_pressure_setpoint_rise_limited_flag, DAT_0040b8c8 fuel_pressure_setpoint_override_additive_flag (both write-only), DAT_00409a78 fuel_pressure_setpoint_rise_limit (3893 counts per pass: no practical limit), DAT_00409a80 / DAT_00409a82 fuel_pressure_setpoint_deadband_fuel_quantity_limit / _engine_speed_limit, DAT_00409a86 fuel_pressure_setpoint_cranking_minimum (307), DAT_00409a6a fuel_pressure_setpoint_running_minimum (512), DAT_00409a7a fuel_pressure_setpoint_maximum (3279 = 160 MPa), DAT_00409a88 fuel_pressure_setpoint_governor_speed_limit_value (2869, used while governor_speed_limit_mode is 1 - park / neutral, vehicle stopped), byte DAT_00409a71 fuel_pressure_setpoint_term_combination_mode (0 sum, 1 minimum; 1 here), DAT_00409a7c / DAT_00409a7e minimum coolant (11520 = 180 F) / intake manifold temperature (4480 = 70 F) for the offset, DAT_0040953e the fault-reaction cap (4095). All are RAM copies of ROM, so no _cal.

Feedback monitor and check A / B variables left out of the rows above (all used only inside their own function), suggested names: 0x40b8e6 cam_timing_position_correction_effective -> fuel_pressure_governor_demand_residual_effective (41 here: DAT_00409aba nonzero replaces the residual); 0x40b8e8 cam_timing_position_correction_scaled -> fuel_pressure_governor_demand_threshold_residual_term (effective x gain / 41, clamped, so equal to the gain here); DAT_0040b90c -> fuel_metering_feedback_low_flag; DAT_00409aba -> fuel_pressure_governor_demand_residual_override (41); DAT_00409abc -> an addend of the threshold (0); byte DAT_00409aa3 -> fuel_metering_feedback_monitor_enable (1); 0x409ab6 / 0x409ab8 (+61 / -61) the pressure error band of the enable. Check B: 0x40b8da cam_timing_correction_base -> fuel_pressure_allowed_decay_model_base; 0x40b8e2 cam_timing_correction_convergence_count / 0x409ab4 _threshold (10) -> fuel_pressure_allowed_decay_below_model_debounce_count / _limit; 0x40b8d8 cam_sync_reference_b_debounce_count / 0x409ab0 _threshold (0) -> fuel_pressure_allowed_decay_check_enable_debounce_count / _limit; 0x40b904 / 0x40b905 the reached / previous flags; DAT_0040b902 below-model flag; DAT_0040b8dc a copy of the model. Check A: 0x40b909 cam_sync_reference_check_enable_flag, 0x40b900 _enable_count, 0x409ac2 _enable_count_threshold (15) are check A's enable gate (-> fuel_pressure_governor_demand_plausibility_check_enable_flag / _enable_count / _enable_count_limit).

protection_fuel_demand_* family: only 0x40b52c, 0x40b52e, 0x40b530 and 0x3fcea8 (rows above) belong to the limiter. About twenty other protection_fuel_demand_* rows (_entry_threshold_cal, _l_threshold_cal, _l4_threshold_cal, _corr_*_cal, _status10 / _status80 thresholds, _snapshot_*, _threshold_derate*_interp_state, _exit_derate*, _limit_derate*, _prev, _tick_snapshot, _working, _correction) are used by other functions and were not checked: leave them. fuel_demand_load_axis (0x40a4ea) is the start value of the ramp but also read elsewhere: left alone. protection_config_flags_b (0x3fd5a8, value 0x801f; bit 1 enables the limiter) lies in the EEPROM mirror (EEPROM 0x126), so it would need _cal and a subject, but its other bits were not checked. Limiter constants with no CSV row (RAM copies of ROM, so no _cal), suggested names: DAT_00408980 fuel_quantity_limit_rail_pressure_shortfall_debounce_limit (2500), DAT_00408982 fuel_quantity_limit_rail_pressure_shortfall_ramp_step (1), DAT_00408984 fuel_quantity_limit_rail_pressure_shortfall_threshold (512 counts = 25 MPa); all used only by the limiter.

Type notes (not proposed as changes by me): 0x3fd0c6 (cam_timing_advance_slew_working) is a dword (8 lwz / stw) typed word, which is why the .cpp shows a leading underscore; 0x409530 is typed word but read as one byte (value 150); 0x409a6d (override value) is a word at an odd address; DAT_0040b8c0 is correctly a dword. engine_timing_arb_status_packed (0x40b932) = byte 0 torque_limit_arb_t_0040a2f6.source_priority, byte 1 the setpoint winning term code, byte 2 engine_timing_arb_byte_16_23, byte 3 engine_timing_arb_byte_24_31 (cm848_updateEngineStatusFlags).

Other readers of fuel_pressure_setpoint that I did not read, so their names are unverified: hpcr_setFaultActiveStatus (0x1e098 / 0x1e1ac), cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor (0xf75c), engine_protection_fuelCorrection_stateMachine (0x530e04), hpcr_injectSystemDiagnostic (0x536ee0). work/tasks/042 pairs 0x49264 and 0x52acfc with fault 303: only 0x49264 sets it. All three monitors (0x52a9ac, 0x52acfc, 0x52b32c) are in one group called by cm848_periodicTaskGroup28_calibration10; 0x52a9ac is disabled, 0x52acfc runs check A only, 0x52b32c runs.
